NO ONLINE CATALOGUE -- homegoods.com is a brand/store-locator site with zero e-commerce. Verified structurally, not inferred: https://www.homegoods.com/sitemap.xml (HTTP 200, 985 <loc> entries) contains 963 /store-details/ pages plus 22 corporate/informational pages (/about, /locator, /faq, /returns, /giftcards, /recalls, /finders-club, /virtualtour, /world-traveler, /findhomeanywhere, /back-to-campus, /dorm-edit, /grand-openings, /photoshare, /howwedoit, /comparisonpricing, /environmental-sustainability, /stay-connected, /tjx-rewards-credit-card, /terms-of-use, /privacy-statement, /all-stores) and NOT ONE product, category or listing URL. The homepage nav contains no shop/department links at all -- only those same informational pages plus outbound links to sibling TJX banners (tjmaxx.tjx.com, marshalls.com, us.homesense.com, sierra.com). The site's own FAQ states the position explicitly: 'Because each store receives thousands of new items each week, it is impossible for us to produce a catalog that could keep up with all our fabulous new styles' and 'we do not provide a service of tracking merchandise.' The /world-traveler editorial page likewise says '*Collection and styles vary by store, please contact your local store for details.' HomeGoods discontinued online shopping in Oct 2023; inventory is in-store only and rotating, so no sub-category has a stable URL or a published product count. Per the brief this is a legitimate empty result rather than a fabricated tree. NAME/DOMAIN DISCREPANCY: the roster company name is 'Tjmaxx' but the assigned domain is homegoods.com -- these are two different TJX banners. company and brand_site are kept exactly as assigned. The T.J.Maxx e-commerce storefront (tjmaxx.tjx.com) is a separate, genuinely shoppable site and was NOT extracted, since the assignment directs extraction from the assigned domain; if the intent was the T.J.Maxx catalogue, this row needs re-running against tjmaxx.tjx.com. ACCESS: direct fetch and r.jina.ai both returned 403 (homegoods.com serves an Akamai/TJX 'securityfailover' page; jina returned a Cloudflare challenge). translate.goog also 403. curl_cffi with impersonate='chrome' returned HTTP 200 on every URL including robots.txt, sitemap.xml and all HTML pages -- the site was fully readable, so this empty result reflects the site's actual content, not a block.
